liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Cumberland Blues** (1 review): Singled out by the reviewer as a standout of the show [8]
- **Good Lovin'** (1 review): Described as tight [16]
- **The Other One** (1 review): This version is divided into four separate tracks in the circulating copy, which the reviewer finds disruptive [11]

## Setlist highlights

- **Little Sadie**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 7 archived performances [18]
- **Long Black Limousine**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 4 archived performances [18]
- Earliest performances in the archive: Monkey & The Engineer, I've Been All Around This World, Mason's Children [18]

## The recordings

- **gd1969-12-19.sbd.clugston.5584.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 16 songs; 117 min; rated 4.43/5 by 7 [1]
- **gd69-12-19.sbd.hanno.9183.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 16 songs; 120 min; rated 2.33/5 by 6 [2]
- **gd1969-12-19.165168.unknown.aud.gen4.miller.t-flac1644**: audience recording; 16 songs; 100 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [3]. Said about its sound: The acoustic first set has no audience sound between songs up to track 6; afterwards the gaps are mostly cut short [3]
- **gd1969-12-19.161117.aud.hanwaker.flac2448**: audience recording; 16 songs; 100 min [4]

## Around the show

- The show opens acoustically because Phil was stuck in traffic, as Bobby tells the crowd [6]
- The acoustic opening set was improvised on the spot rather than planned [9]
- Phil being stuck somewhere may have been a way to float going acoustic without confrontation, since members were repeatedly delayed that month [12]
- The band teased Wake Up Little Susie, but Jerry admitted he didn't know all the words [16]
- Only four songs were acoustic, an accidental mini-set because Phil was late [17]
- Listed as the New Old Fillmore, with Osceola and Rhythm Dukes named as other acts [3]
- Reviews of the 12-26 show call that one the first acoustic set, which conflicts with this show's acoustic opening [6]
- The reviewer sees the acoustic shift as almost the opposite of Dylan's controversial move to electric [12]
- The reviewer recalls an earlier 1969 show where a late or missing member also led to several acoustic songs [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1969-12-19.sbd.clugston.5584.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Scott Clugston; source: 7" Master Soundboard Reels > Cassette > DAT > CDR [1]
- **gd69-12-19.sbd.hanno.9183.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Uli Teute, Hanno Bunjes, Scott Clugston; source: Soundboard patched by Audience [2]. Also: The soundboard used was the Scott Clugston seed; Casey Jones from 1:05 to 4:21 is patched by H.B. using an audience tape from Uli [2]
- **gd1969-12-19.165168.unknown.aud.gen4.miller.t-flac1644**: taped by uli teute aka hanwaker 2022-12; source: AUD 4th generation cassette played back on NAK LX-5 -> Edirol R04 (@ WAV 24/48) >HD -> Audacity (edit) -> WAV 24/48 > Flac 8 [3]. Also: This is a fourth-generation audience recording, filed under Miller, with an unknown taper [3]
- **gd1969-12-19.161117.aud.hanwaker.flac2448**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Uli Teute; source: AUD 4th generation [4]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Fillmore, Dec. '69 Poster](https://www.dead.net/archives/1969/artwork/fillmore-dec-69-poster) [19]
